commands.name: jobs
commands.description: Open the Jobs pane (long-running jobs and disk space)

commands.name: watch
commands.description: Watch a log file in the Jobs pane

commands.name: unwatch
commands.description: Stop watching a job (by label or id), or clear finished ones

tools.name: jobs_list
tools.description: List the long-running jobs job-watch follows: background Bash tasks, detached nohup launches, and anything added with jobs_watch. For each: its state (running, quiet, stalled, or finished with its exit code), how long since it last wrote output, progress and ETA when its log shows them, its last log line and its log path. Call this to follow or wait for long-running work instead of writing `until … sleep` / `while … sleep` loops or running `ps`: background Bash jobs (run_in_background: true) are picked up automatically the moment they start.

tools.name: jobs_watch
tools.description: Add a process or a log file to the jobs job-watch follows, so jobs_list can report on it: `pid` (followed until it exits), `log` (a file whose growth, progress figures and last line are read), or both; `name` labels it and `quietMinutes` says after how long without output it counts as stalled. Only needed for work started outside this session's Bash (another session, a cron job, a pid you were given): background Bash tasks (run_in_background: true) and `nohup … > log 2>&1 &` launches are picked up automatically. It does not start commands: run those with Bash. Use it instead of `ps` or sleep loops.

tools.name: jobs_unwatch
tools.description: Stop following a job, by the name or id jobs_list prints; `done` removes every finished job, `all` removes them all.

children: No jobs yet. Background commands and nohup launches that write to a log show up here; /watch adds any log file.
